context:

description:
## Problem
The TPC specifications never check the answers of the measured power and throughput streams (their parameters come from an unknown seed). BenchBox asks those streams for exact answers, and an early return in benchbox/core/validation/query_validation.py (~32-55, ~260-273) skips every TPC-DS query whose parameters differ from one reference set, so seeded and official TPC-DS runs can never be validated. Two wrong answers sit in the stored corpus recorded as passed (TPC-DS q93 empty at SF 0.1 on three platforms; TPC-H Q15 empty on one platform).

## Change (owner decisions 1 and 2, 2026-11-25)
- Delete the blanket TPC-DS exclusion and the thread-local reference-seed flag. One row decision function, shared by the SQL path and the DataFrame path (benchbox/core/dataframe/query_validation.py ~188-240), in this order: LIMIT and one-row checks; exact reference for these exact parameters (keyed by dsqgen RNGSEED and STREAMS file index, or qgen seed, never by stream number); invariant count; enumerated range (TPC-H SF 1 only, tpch_results.py ~20-29); must return rows; otherwise a documented 'parameter sensitive:' skip.
- LIMIT and one-row bounds derived once from the templates into a small table, checked by a unit test against every template's generated SQL.
- invariant_counts and never_empty derived from a recorded sample of at least 512 draws per scale at SF 0.01, 0.1 and 1, covering spread random seeds through the per-template and STREAMS paths, the seedless seeds, and load-end-time-style seeds; DuckDB runs the sample, DataFusion must agree on a 64-draw subset. Stored in an integrity section of each reference file with full provenance.
- References apply only when benchmark.data_generation_hash equals the reference stamp; otherwise a documented 'reference data differs' skip and the LIMIT/one-row checks still run. A CI guard fails when the generator stamp changes without regenerated references.
- Row evidence gains check (exact, invariant, range, never_empty, structural) and bound; validation.stream_checks records the reference files applied.
- A violation makes the row FAILED, so the run is failed, refused on both paths and never official. The failure message names the statement, check kind, bound, sample size and data stamp.
- Remove the current TPC-DS subscale sensitivity list (query_validation.py ~24-29) and the SF 1 special case in _apply_tpcds_validation_mode (~176-179); stop using the TPC-DS SF 1 answer sets for stream rows (they move to the qualification test in crr-v3). Keep the TPC-H Q16 tolerance and the enumerated TPC-H SF 1 ranges; no other observed min-max range.
- Bump the result schema 2.6 to 2.7 with a top-level validation object holding validation.stream_checks, and the row-evidence fields check and bound; record it in docs/internal/adr/adr-result-bundle-json-schema.md and the schema specs and models. Coordinate the version with tpc-full-spec-result-schema so both do not claim it.
- Update docs/agent/maintainer-bundles.md (TPC-DS statements, and the adjudication procedure below) and tests/unit/core/throughput/test_throughput_query_correctness.py. Do not reintroduce the staged text 'throughput rows and other seeds are skipped'.

## Decision gates
- If DuckDB and DataFusion disagree on any statement during generation, stop and report the statement and draws; do not pick one.
- If the new checks fail any stored row at a reference scale other than the known TPC-DS q93 (SF 0.1, three cloud platforms), TPC-H Q15 (DataFusion 53) and the two early DataFrame TPC-DS SF 1 files, stop and report before landing.
- Generation is heavy work (about 1 to 1.5 hours): make heavy-run only, announced.
- A disputed failure from an invariant or must-return-rows check is settled by re-running the recorded statement text on DuckDB at the same data stamp (owner decision 2, 2026-11-25). If DuckDB agrees with the platform, add that seed to the sample, regenerate the references and re-run the result; if it disagrees, the platform answer is wrong. Never edit a stored file or relax a check by hand.

## Guardrails (apply to every step of this plan)
- Fix the root cause for every platform and benchmark. No rule, check, exception, label or test may name a platform or a version matrix; only the pvm items may name Polars, and only to run and stage that run's files.
- Never edit a stored result file. Stored outcomes change only through the rule; any change shows in the committed snapshot diff (scripts/corpus_compliance_snapshot.py) and is explained per bundle in the pull request body.
- No new stored class value. No reader decides anything from benchmark.compliance_class, conformance_class or summary.tpc_metrics.suppressed.
- One implementation per concept: reuse existing helpers; make duplicate-check-delta stays at +0; no second copy of the rule, the roll-up, the row decision or the qualification comparator.
- No explanatory comments or docstrings (make comment-policy-check). User-facing changes add a changelog.d fragment; never edit CHANGELOG.md.
- Heavy work only through make heavy-run, after make heavy-status, with command, maximum run time and log path announced first. No live cloud runs. Never touch the lock, set BENCHBOX_SKIP_TEST_LOCK, BENCHBOX_HEAVY_ADMIT=force or BENCHBOX_HEAVY_WATCHDOG=off.
- Work in a linked worktree on the step's feature batch. Each batch is one pull request; run the local review before opening it; fix hosted-review findings. If the hosted review cannot complete, split the pull request so a reviewer can read it (owner, 2026-11-24). Never post a stand-in or adjudication, except on published-results pull requests, which follow the owner decision of 2026-11-24: an independent review with no Critical or Required findings, then a stand-in that cites it.
- Paths and line numbers were read on 2026-11-25 at the corpus rule head; re-read before editing and report drift instead of guessing.
- At a decision gate, follow the recorded owner decision. If its stop condition is met, stop and report to the owner; never substitute a different decision.
- Owner decisions: crr-00-corpus-rule-remediation-plan context, entries of 2026-11-22, 2026-11-24 and 2026-11-25. Design: the spec-faithful validation plan summarized in crr-00 (qualification test, integrity checks, official-mode sequence).
